newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee market uncertain, no rush to buy.
newsitem.headline: German coffee market uncertain, no rush to buy.

text.p: German coffee roasters were uncertain about the direction of futures after a bout of profit-taking ended last week's spectacular run-up to 20-year highs, traders said on Monday.
"The price slide may continue but on the other hand we've just moved into the Brazilian frost season," one said.
"The industry is in no hurry to buy against July unless it is absolutely necessary."
New York July arabicas ended at 276.40 cents/lb on Friday, down 38.40, but at a hefty premium over September at 238.30.

Traders said lack of interest in Europe and the United States in Colombia's June export allocation showed the industry's cover for summer roastings may be better than previously thought. Consumers had taken vast amounts of Brazilian new crop in recent weeks, they added.
The roasting industry was still trying for enforce higher retail prices in a hostile environment because of competitive pressures and stagnant consumption.
Importers reported some sales of Brazilian and Central American new crop as well as East African and Asian arabicas wherever origin differentials were cut.
Robustas sold for dates up to the end of the year but activity lagged that seen in recent weeks.
Brazils for July/August shipment cost $257 per 50 kg fob, up $40 on the week, with Guatemalan hb at $349, up $46.
Vietnam robustas were offered at $117 cif, up $24.50.
